title: Ozone therapy (O(2)-O(3)) alleviates the progression of early intervertebral disc degeneration via the inhibition of oxidative stress and the interception of the PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
authors: Elmounedi, Najah; Bahloul, Walid; Kharrat, Abdelkader; Horchani, Mabrouk; Ben Jannet, Hichem; Racem Guidara, Ahmed; Keskes, Hassib
one_liner_zh: 该文研究臭氧疗法对椎间盘退变的缓解作用，涉及分子对接但对象为臭氧与PI3K/COX-2蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) stands for the most frequent cause of low back pain. Finding a cure for this disease is an important challenge as current conservative treatments and surgical interventions fail to bring a solution to this disease. Ozone therapy (O(2)-O(3)) has yielded outstanding outcomes in intervertebral disc pathology. The ozone's efficacy in the treatment of IDD remains unconfirmed. This study aimed to assess the effectiveness of intradiscal ozone injection on IDD induced in a rat. Effects of ozone therapy on the viability of nucleus pulposus cells were evaluated by CCK-8 assays. Macrophage immunoreactivity was detected by immunohistochemical, the expression of collagen type II was evaluated by western blot, and measurement of oxidative stress parameters was realized. Molecular docking studies were carried out in order to predict the interaction formed between O(3) and the target enzymes, on the one hand, O(3) with PI3K and, on the other hand, O(3) with COX-2. IRM, X-ray, hematoxylin-eosin, and bleu alcian staining were realized to assess the therapeutic impacts of ozone in the puncture-induced rat model of IDD. In vivo, O(3) ameliorated the IDD in the early stage of this disease. It was also displayed in molecular docking that O(3) might bind to PI3K to suppress the PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB signaling pathway. This study's results show that the O(3) should be administered at the low grade of IDD and at an early stage because it cannot restore the advanced inflammatory alteration of the IVD. Our results corroborated also that O(3) inhibits the progression of IDD via the PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB signaling pathway, which supports O(3) as an effective therapeutic option for treating IDD.
abstract_zh: 椎间盘退变（IDD）是腰痛最常见的病因。寻找治愈该疾病的方法是一项重要挑战，因为目前的保守治疗和手术干预均未能解决此问题。臭氧疗法（O(2)-O(3)）在椎间盘病理中已取得显著成效。然而，臭氧在治疗IDD中的疗效仍未得到确认。本研究旨在评估椎间盘内臭氧注射对大鼠诱导性IDD的有效性。通过CCK-8实验评估臭氧疗法对髓核细胞活力的影响。采用免疫组织化学检测巨噬细胞免疫反应性，通过蛋白质印迹法评估II型胶原蛋白的表达，并进行氧化应激参数的测量。进行了分子对接研究，以预测O(3)与靶酶之间的相互作用，一方面为O(3)与PI3K，另一方面为O(3)与COX-2。通过IRM、X射线、苏木精-伊红染色和阿尔辛蓝染色，评估臭氧在穿刺诱导的大鼠IDD模型中的治疗效果。在体内实验中，O(3)在疾病早期改善了IDD。分子对接结果也显示，O(3)可能结合PI3K以抑制PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB信号通路。本研究结果表明，O(3)应在IDD低级别和早期阶段给药，因为它无法恢复椎间盘（IVD）的晚期炎症改变。我们的结果还证实，O(3)通过PI3K/Akt/NF-kappaB信号通路抑制IDD的进展，这支持O(3)作为治疗IDD的有效治疗选择。
